findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The ice machine baffle and inner surfaces were observed to have soil accumulation. The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and instructed to clean the baffle as well as the inner surfaces and maintain the ice machine free of soil buildup. Ensure the ice machine baffle and inner surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will follow up on March 9, 2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Strawberry fruit jam labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” was observed on a shelf. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed as well as educated and the jam was voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” are kept in the cooler and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in all the coolers. The PIC was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Soil and debris accumulations were observed on the dish holder by the three-compartment sink.
2. Debris accumulation was observed in the utensils holder under the dish holder by the three-compartment sink.

The PIC was instructed to have those surfaces clean. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 The facility has a routine for making and using small batches of boba. The boba still needs to have a time as a control marking of some sort. Discussed using a white board or the tile back splash. The boba on the counter top did not have a time as control tag. Make sure to mark in use boba with 4 hour time tag and use or discard any left after the 4 hours. Boba was marked.

(A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11:The counter top edge piece to the right of the hand sink on the line is no longer sealed to the counter top. Caulk seal behind the prep sink on the make line area is molded. Remove the seal, clean and replace.

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) No certified food protection manager (CFPM) on duty at time of inspection. Employees are food handler certified. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all operational hours. There are three certified food protection manager’s licensed; however, there is infrequency with how often the CFPM’s are at the facility. During today’s inspection, the main manager/owner who is a CFPM was stated to be gone until the weekend due to being out of town. Provided class list to encourage taking the course and exam. Another CFPM should be licensed to have enough to cover being present during operational hours. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 7/22/19, 6/30/20, 10/27/21, and 9/20/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

Observed all ice cream time controlled utensils to be rinsed in the handsink. Wash, rinse, sanitize in 3 compartment sink every 4 hours. Not taking place. Do not used handsink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

Observed both employees to dump ice cream tong water in handsink and rinse tongs. There is a language barrier. Attempted to explain handsink is for handwashing only. COS. Items need to be washed, rinsed, sanitized in 3 compartment sink. Observed PIC to dampen and ring in-use rag in handsink. Handsink is for handwashing ONLY.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed no hand washing before engaging in food behaviors. Inspector witnessed both employees to not wash hands prior to starting to make drinks. Discussed with all staff during inspection. Ensure appropriate hand washing before food engagement - soap, hot water, paper towels to dry hands. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off the faucets in order to not cross contamination hands. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/20/20 and 10/27/21.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sanitization bucket to be too low - 100 ppm of quat. Sanitizer concentration should be 200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonium. Facility has test strips and Inspector noted one employee actively testing the, “sanitize”, basin of the 3 compartment sink. Ensure frequent changes of the sani bucket to maintain 200-400 ppm of sanitizer. Discussed with employees. COS.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 

Observed a set of tongs within a water with basin on top of the cold holding of the rolled ice cream machine. Inspector probed one employee about the process utilized regarding the tongs and water. Employee stated they change the water several times a day and rinse off the tongs. It is correct to be changing the water several times a day (every 4 hours), but the tongs and basin should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours as well or replaced by new tongs and basin (food contact surface). A policy has been created with SCDPH in the past for ice cream utensils (see attachment in CDP). Historically, this facility was utilizing time control, then changed to putting ice cream utensils inside the top prep cooler near the rolled ice cream machines. It appears the time control policy is being utilized again. Ensure a time stamp system for every 4 hours to wash, rinse, sanitize and that all staff is aware of this operational procedure. Inspector will follow-up on 9/30/22.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed several coolers not to have thermometers within. Most coolers at the facility have an outside digital thermometer, but no internal thermometer. Ensure all coolers have a thermometer within to measure the temperature of the cold holding unit.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Observed the 3 compartment sink to have a constant drink despite pressing back on both faucet handles. A minor leak appears to be dripping below the 3 compartment sink. Ensure repairs are made to the triple sink.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed all the cabinets in the ice cream prep area to have exposed/bare wood. Seal with paint or clear coat. Ensure the cabinet bases and smooth and easily cleanable. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no CFPM present during inspection. PIC is food handler’s licensed. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all hours of operation. The facility has 2 certified food protection manager’s that are licensed; however, these CFPM’s are not frequently at the facility. Ensure 1-2 more CFPM’s are licensed before the next routine inspection. Provided paperwork for taking the classes. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/30/20 and 7/22/19.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements during inspection. Provided new copy. Ensure this document is reviewed and all employee’s sign a copy. Keep within a public health folder or binder. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/30/20.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed PIC to done gloves before engaging in food prep and not wash hands before donning gloves. Inspector stopped PIC and kindly asked to wash hands. Education was provided regarding appropriate hand washing techniques. Discussed turning off faucet with a barrier such as a paper towel. Ensure hand washing is performed before donning gloves and returning to food preparation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/30/20.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple areas of facility where in-use rags were present and not in a sanitization bucket with solution. Discussed changing practices with PIC. When rags are not in-use, they should be within the sanitization bucket with accurate concentration of sanitizer. A new sani bucket was made and rags were placed within the bucket. Cease practice of leaving in-use rags on counters. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/30/20 and 7/22/19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

(REPEAT) Observed no functioning sanitization bucket during inspection. Facility is just placing in-use rags within an empty bucket. Cease practice. Provided education on proper sanitization bucket procedure and in-use rag procedures (see violation #41). Quat - 200 ppm. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/30/20.
